name: Perito Moreno Glacier
description: One of the world's most awe-inspiring natural wonders, the Perito Moreno Glacier stretches 30 km and towers 60 metres above Lake Argentino.
highlights: Watch massive ice blocks calve into the turquoise lake
Walk the elevated boardwalks for panoramic glacier views
Take an ice trekking adventure on the glacier surface
Witness the spectacular rupture cycle every 4–5 years
Spot Andean condors soaring above the ice field
tips: Arrive early to beat the crowds and get the best light for photos.
Bring layered clothing — the glacial winds can be very cold even in summer.
Book ice trekking tours at least 48 hours in advance.
The park entrance fee is ~$25 USD for foreigners.

name: Buenos Aires
description: The vibrant capital of Argentina blends European architecture with Latin passion — tango halls, world-class steakhouses, colourful La Boca, and a buzzing nightlife.
highlights: Explore the colourful Caminito street in La Boca neighbourhood
Watch a live tango show in San Telmo or Palermo
Visit the iconic Recoleta Cemetery — final resting place of Eva Perón
Stroll the wide Avenida 9 de Julio — the world's widest boulevard
Dine on a world-famous Argentine asado
tips: Use the Subte (metro) to get around — it's cheap and efficient.
Avoid peak summer (December–February) as the city can get very humid.
Many restaurants don't open for dinner until 9 PM — embrace the late schedule.
Exchange money at official exchange houses (casas de cambio) for the best rates.

name: Iguazú Falls
description: Wider than Niagara and taller than Victoria Falls, Iguazú is a network of 275 waterfalls spanning nearly 3 km across the Argentine-Brazilian border.
highlights: Stand at the Garganta del Diablo (Devil's Throat) viewpoint
Take a zodiac boat ride under the spray of the falls
Spot toucans, coatis, and butterflies on jungle trails
Visit both the Argentine and Brazilian sides for full views
Sunrise visit for golden light and zero crowds
tips: Wear a waterproof poncho or bring a full change of clothes for the boat ride.
The Argentine side has more trails and closer waterfall access than the Brazilian side.
Go early in the morning — the park gets extremely busy by noon.
The park is inside Iguazú National Park; entry is ~$30 USD for foreigners.

name: Mendoza Wine Region
description: Argentina's wine capital nestled at the foot of the Andes produces some of the world's finest Malbec. Cycle through vineyards and taste wine with mountain views.
highlights: Cycle the vineyard routes of Maipú and Luján de Cuyo
Taste world-class Malbec at boutique bodegas
Enjoy an olive oil tasting paired with local cheeses
Day trip to Aconcagua — highest peak in the Americas
Visit during Vendimia harvest festival (March)
tips: Rent a bicycle in Maipú — the flat vineyard routes are perfect for cycling.
Book winery tours in advance, especially during harvest season.
The city itself has beautiful tree-lined streets and excellent restaurants.
Pair your Malbec with a local empanada for an authentic experience.

name: Bariloche & Patagonia
description: The Swiss-alpine-meets-Patagonia town on the shores of Nahuel Huapi Lake — hike, ski, kayak, and indulge in legendary Argentine chocolate.
highlights: Hike the Cerro Catedral circuit for Andean panoramas
Ski or snowboard at Cerro Catedral ski resort (June–Sept)
Kayak on the crystal-clear Nahuel Huapi Lake
Drive the scenic Ruta de los Siete Lagos
Sample artisan chocolate at Bariloche's famous chocolate shops
tips: The cable car to Cerro Catedral summit is worth every peso for the views.
Book accommodation months in advance for ski season (July–August).
Try the local cerveza artesanal (craft beer) scene alongside the chocolate.
Colectivo buses connect most key spots — a car is not required.

name: Salta & the Northwest
description: Known as 'La Linda' (The Beautiful), Salta enchants with colonial baroque architecture, Andean culture, the spectacular Quebrada de Humahuaca, and the cloud-forest Yungas.
highlights: Explore the UNESCO-listed Quebrada de Humahuaca valley
Ride the Train to the Clouds — the world's highest railway
Visit the baroque Cathedral and MAAM museum in Salta city
Taste traditional Andean foods: humitas, tamales, and locro
See the rainbow-striped Cerro de los Siete Colores in Purmamarca
tips: Altitude sickness can affect visitors — acclimatize slowly and drink mate coca tea.
Hire a local guide for the Quebrada de Humahuaca for the best cultural context.
The Tren a las Nubes (Train to the Clouds) requires advance booking.
Markets in Purmamarca sell excellent artisan textiles and silver jewellery.
